extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, media critics, and students of communication/political economy
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes Noam Chomsky's 'five filters' (ownership, advertising, media elite, flak, common enemy) as a framework for evaluating how mainstream mass media select and shape news. Useful for critiquing news outlets, newsroom practices, and news-homepage selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass media firms are big corporations, often parts of larger conglomerates; their end game is profit, which shapes their output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because corporate owners prioritize profit, critical journalism is subordinated to corporate needs and interests. Evaluate outlets by who owns them and how ownership structures and profit motives might bias coverage or limit critical reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising finances media because consumer payments don't cover costs; advertisers pay for audiences, not just the media product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how dependence on advertiser revenue shapes content: the media sell audiences to advertisers, so programming and editorial choices may favor what keeps audiences attractive to advertisers rather than what informs the public. Watch for content skewed toward advertiser-friendly topics and avoidance of material that might alienate advertisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: The media elite (sourcing and institutional ties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment manages the media via close relationships: governments, corporations, and big institutions feed scoops, official accounts, and 'experts' to journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how reliance on official sources and an embedded elite of experts produces complicity rather than a check on power. Evaluate sourcing patterns, the prevalence of official narratives, who is repeatedly given platform, and whether alternative voices are marginalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flak
rubrics_metrics.description: When journalists, whistleblowers, or sources stray from consensus or challenge power, they face 'flak'—organized pushback that discredits sources, trashes stories, and diverts conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how criticism of dominant narratives is met with pressure, discrediting campaigns, legal threats, or coordinated media responses. Use evidence of flak to explain why dissenting stories are marginalized and to assess the resilience of critical reporting in a given outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: The common enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturing consent requires a common enemy or bogeyman (examples: Communism, terrorists, immigrants) that helps corral public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for discursive patterns that construct or emphasize external threats to unify audiences or justify policy positions. Assess how repeatedly framing groups or ideas as enemies shapes news selection, prioritization, and emotional tone to manufacture consent for particular policies or power arrangements.
